prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1245; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot between the insured vehicle and a third-party vehicle. Insured reports the other driver backed into the insured's rear quarter panel while exiting a space. Initial photos requested. Police report not filed as no injuries were reported at the scene.

Entry 2: Claimant contacted the office through counsel. Attorney letter of representation received and logged. All further communication to be directed to the attorney's office. Claimant reports a wrist injury sustained in the collision and states treatment is ongoing. Medical records and authorization forms requested through counsel.

Entry 3: Medical documentation received from the claimant's provider. Diagnosis indicates a fracture of the wrist, with immobilization and a follow-up consultation scheduled. Records reviewed and forwarded for medical bill review. Reserve adjusted to reflect bodily injury exposure. Counsel notified that the claim file is under review.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspected at the repair facility. Damage to rear quarter panel, bumper cover, and tail lamp assembly confirmed and consistent with the reported loss. Repair estimate received and under review. Liability is being evaluated based on the parking lot surveillance footage requested from the property owner, which has not yet been received.

Entry 5: Follow-up call placed to claimant's counsel regarding outstanding medical records and the status of the wrist treatment. Counsel advised that a settlement demand will follow once the treatment course is complete. File remains open pending receipt of the demand package, the property footage, and the final repair invoice. Next diary review set for thirty days out.
